figures.caption: Figure 2: Rank-percentile accuracy: fraction of events on which the chosen action falls within the top X% of the ranked action set. The real player (dashed) leads every VLM at every threshold, and every VLM leads RANDOM (dotted); all curves meet at 100% when X = 100. The comparison is purely ordinal, value magnitudes do not enter.

Figure 1: The SportD task. From the run-up clip, freeze-frame, and top-down map (lettered circles for players, a gold star for the player on the ball, an arrow for the attacking direction), the VLM chooses one action: a pass to a lettered teammate or a shot. Bottom right: the four VLMs’ and the real player’s choices, green if optimal and red otherwise. Here one VLM, GPT 5.6 Sol, finds the optimal pass; the others, and the player (who shot), do not.

Figure 3: Progression of the chosen pass. (a) Mean goal-ward gain (metres the ball moves toward the attacking goal): the optimal pass advances it ∼9m, the real players ∼1m, and the VLMs near zero or backward. (b) Share of passes that go forward at all. VLMs decline the penetrating pass just as they decline the shot.

Table 1: Main results (n = 478), with the real player as the baseline and RANDOM and ORACLE as floor and ceiling. The ORACLE always plays a⋆ and so scores perfectly by construction. Every VLM lands between random and the player on every metric. Top-X% is the fraction of choices ranking among the best X% of available actions. Regret and skill follow Eqs. 3, 4.
